comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formally adopted Faculty of Science EER; standard single bachelor
comparator.route: Natuur- en Sterrenkunde, ordinary 180-EC bachelor without optional advanced astronomy minor or dual degree
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted EER, Articles 7.3–7.5, prescribes 60 EC first-year courses, 69 EC compulsory second/third-year courses, 39 EC non-overlapping eligible elective space (which may include a 15–30 EC minor), and a 12-EC Bachelorstage Natuur- en Sterrenkunde final research project: 60+69+39+12=180. First-year physics/practical/data course NWI-NP017E is 9 EC, replacing the older 6-EC lab and 3-EC data components; the current route does not count both. The English Writing Skills in Academia is the first-listed allowed writing-course choice. The 30-EC Advanced Astronomy minor is optional and its old form closes to registration at the end of 2026–27; selecting it creates a specific 6-EC laboratory exemption and is therefore not silently added to the general route. The 225-EC Mathematics and Physics dual bachelor and transitional cohorts are separate. General 0-EC RADAr requirements are not counted in the 180 EC. The formally named route is the standard Dutch-taught single bachelor, even though individual courses may be in English.

routeSelection.route: Natuur- en Sterrenkunde, ordinary 180-EC bachelor without optional advanced astronomy minor or dual degree
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target denotes the ordinary accredited Physics and Astronomy bachelor. The advanced astronomy minor and mathematics double degree are optional, distinct commitments; preserving the 39-EC choice space is the neutral general reconstruction.

core: Mathematics, programming, modelling and data analysis for physical-science questions
Physical Earth systems, materials, energy and environmental processes
Measurement, imaging, statistical analysis and scientific observation
Neurobiology, perception, cognition and the target’s Neurophysics direction
Independent scientific inquiry and critical assessment of evidence
questions: How can mathematical models, observation and data explain dynamic physical systems, materials and environments?
How do biological systems produce perception, cognition and behaviour, and how can those systems be modelled quantitatively?

candidates.label: Astronomy & astrophysics
candidates.assessment: UCR has image processing, Earth observation and quantitative methods, but no astronomy, stellar or planetary physics, relativity, gravitation or observational-astronomy sequence. These methods cannot sustain a complete astronomy curriculum.

candidates.label: Fundamental & experimental physics
candidates.assessment: UCR lacks mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermodynamics, quantum theory, relativity and an experimental-physics laboratory sequence. Mathematics, modelling and Earth science are related contributions, not replacements for this cumulative core.

candidates.label: Atomic & molecular physics
candidates.assessment: Biochemistry and computational methods do not supply atomic structure, molecular spectroscopy, quantum mechanics or the required physics laboratory foundation.

candidates.label: High-energy & particle physics
candidates.assessment: UCR offers no particle physics, gravitational physics, quantum field theory or preceding mechanics and electromagnetism sequence.

candidates.label: Solid-state & condensed-matter physics
candidates.assessment: Environmental materials courses do not provide electronic structure, crystallography, quantum mechanics, solid-state physics or experimental condensed-matter work.

candidates.label: Physics education
candidates.assessment: UCR lacks the undergraduate physics content and physics didactics needed for a coherent teaching-physics route; the limitation is academic preparation, not qualification alone.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, data & physical Earth systems
alternatives.labelReason: Thirteen Earth, environmental, resource and energy courses combine with six mathematics courses and four programming/data courses; the label reflects those proportions and does not claim physics or astronomy.
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, dynamic-systems analysis, probability, programming and data methods to study the Earth, climate, natural hazards, materials, resources and energy systems. This is a quantitative related-fields response to the target’s interest in physical laws, materials and the environment; it contains no mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics or astronomy sequence.
progression: Earth-science, sustainability, programming, mathematical and data foundations precede advanced calculus, numerical and linear-systems work, Earth observation, environmental modelling, biogeochemistry, resources, energy-system design and the applied research project. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Neuroscience, perception & quantitative modelling
alternatives.labelReason: Neurobiology, perception, cognition, development and biological mechanisms form the subject core, supported by eleven mathematics, programming, data and research-method courses; the label does not represent these as neurophysics.
alternatives.concept: Develop the target’s explicit Neurophysics direction through neurobiology, perception, cognition, physiology, cellular mechanisms and human development, supported by mathematics, programming, statistics, modelling, imaging and research synthesis. This is a neuroscience-and-modelling route: it does not supply the mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum theory or specialist physical measurement that define neurophysics at Radboud.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming and mathematical foundations precede perception, physiology, experimental statistics, molecular-cell biology, numerical and linear-systems modelling, advanced cognition, genetics, psycholinguistics and research synthesis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
traceOverrides: studies signals, transfer functions, state-space models and differential equations for quantitative analysis of dynamic systems
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme applies mathematics and data to Earth systems, materials, resources and energy. This programme makes brain biology, perception and cognition the organising centre and uses quantitative courses in that biological context. The routes share nine non-PPD courses and differ by fourteen courses / 105 EC in each direction, well above the 30-EC floor.

selection.assessment: The quantitative Earth-systems programme is the strongest complete related-fields response to the target’s evidenced mathematics, programming and physical-environment interests. Neurophysics is an explicit structured direction and supports a genuinely different neuroscience-and-modelling programme. The next direction, astronomy and astrophysics, cannot be built without astronomy, relativity and a physics sequence; atomic, high-energy, solid-state and teaching-physics directions fail for corresponding specialist-content gaps. Production therefore stops at two.

blocks: Both directly develop programming for scientific work; UCR does not supply the surrounding physics curriculum.
Both develop foundational calculus and mathematical methods, while Radboud’s course sits inside a cumulative physics sequence.

notes.text: Radboud Physics and Astronomy requires cumulative mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermodynamics, quantum theory, relativity, specialist physics and experimental laboratories. UCR can combine mathematics and data with physical Earth systems, or pursue the target’s Neurophysics direction through neuroscience and quantitative modelling. These are related-fields responses: neither reproduces the physics-and-astronomy curriculum, and UCR offers no astronomy or experimental-physics sequence.
